title: Combinatorial invariance of Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials
coverage: I read all of the LaTeX: 01-introduction, 02-background, 03-dihedral, 04-localization, 05-comparison (which includes the Section 6 induction) and the README. The family-168 board was empty when I started. I checked each of the following by hand. (1) Reduction to finite rank. (2) The reflection-faithful realization, and the sign criterion for rho. (3) Dihedral plane subgroups: the rank-two argument, the coset identification and the inversion-count formula. (4) The dihedral shape lemma, and graph reconstruction through the four-layer closure rule, including the three-edge refinement by descent induction. (5) Transport of relative dihedral intervals (Prop 3.x). (6) The midpoint-label order (1<3<... then ...<-3<-1). (7) The planar sum identity sum_D k_D(e) = (d-1)/2. (8) Relative flabbiness after localization. (9) The descending Braden–MacPherson-style decomposition over R = A_p into structure sheaves O_c. (10) The edge-image inclusion I ⊆ f_e J, checked through height-one primes of A/(alpha) and the lattice lemma; this includes the valuation bookkeeping and the fact that f_e's factors from other planes are units at the prime. (11) The Hilbert-series bound at each step: I verified the identity T·D_y algebraically. (12) That the matrix product counts label-decreasing paths, and that Dyer's path formula gives R~'(T) at q^{-1}. (13) The reciprocity squeeze Delta(q) <= Delta(1/q) in both directions, which forces Delta = 0 by the degree bound. (14) That every coordinate becomes an equality, so the telescoping deficits vanish and I = f_e J. (15) That Schanuel's lemma plus graded Nakayama gives freeness, and that the induction never relies on freeness at u itself. Computations: a Python script checked the later-edge count lemma h_x - h_y = k_D(e) on every arrow e and top c in the infinite dihedral group (indices up to 9) and in I2(m) for m = 2..8, under both angular orders, with 0 failures across thousands of cases. A numerical linear-algebra check (up to degree 6) confirmed that the dihedral structure sheaves O_c are flabby, as Lemma loc:models requires. I ran it with real root labels for kappa in {1, 1.5, 3} and for cos(pi/m) with m = 3..6. I accepted the following cited inputs without re-deriving them: Theorem bg:bmp (the Fiebig/Braden–MacPherson/Elias–Williamson sheaf properties for arbitrary Coxeter systems over this realization); the convention chase for the grading normalization, Prop bg:normalization (consistent with a hand check in a smooth dihedral case); and Dyer's path formula.
main_claim: Take any two Coxeter systems and Bruhat intervals [u,b] and [u',b'] in them. If the intervals are isomorphic as abstract posets, then P_{u,b} = P'_{u',b'}, and all KL polynomials and R-polynomials on their subintervals also agree. This is the full combinatorial invariance conjecture, for arbitrary (including infinite and non-crystallographic) Coxeter groups.
sibling_notes: The hive:oai_math:review:fam:168 board was empty when I checked, so no sibling reports existed and none affected this audit. I posted a no_gap_found summary there.
